coreJob.statement: Remove what my files say about me, without surprises, and let me see what changed.

clauses.text: Users reported or asked about identifying data: geolocation fields, the PC name and user name, face tags, and the user name and project name from a design tool.
Users reported surprises after cleaning: photos rotated, print resolution reset, a modified original with Save as copy on, a changed modification date.
Users asked to see what was removed and were unsure when the count read 0.
The sentence is the brand book's job statement, pinned at the recorded commit.

claims.text: Has a folder or a large set to clean in one sitting.
Users asked for whole folders and sub-folders, and for multiple files at once.
After a large batch, finding the results and telling cleaned from failed files is a need the maintainer's own issues describe.
One failure hides among hundreds of successes.

redFlags.text: One failed file stops, or is hidden among, the rest of the batch.
A batch summary that counts already-clean and failed files the same way, so the two cannot be told apart.
Rows that cannot be told apart: long or duplicate names, no folder context.

claims.text: Has RAW, TIFF or print files whose masters must come out as they went in, minus the private fields.
Users reported print resolution reset to 96, RAF files that would not open after cleaning, and asked to keep only the colour profile or the modification date.
Preserve resolution is a shipped setting.
Preserve color profile is a shipped setting.
Preserve orientation is a shipped setting.
Preserve modification date is a shipped setting.
A master that is damaged, or silently altered, is lost work.

redFlags.text: A cleaned RAW file that no longer opens, or an original modified while Save as copy is on.
A preserve setting reported as kept when the field was not kept (resolution, colour, HDR gain map).

claims.text: Has a photo or file about to be posted, sent or sold.
Users reported photos rotated or flipped after cleaning, and two asked for the rotation to be kept.
A user dropped an image and saw nothing happen, in two reports.
One user described themselves as not very tech-oriented.
If the tool misleads, the file leaves with its metadata still inside.

redFlags.text: A cleaned photo comes back rotated or flipped by default.
A dropped image that shows nothing on screen.
Copy that uses fear to sell, naming what could happen to a person instead of what is removed.

source.section: Inclusive language, and writing for translation

claims.text: Has a file whose origin or location would identify someone, and must hand it over or publish it.
Users reported identifying fields they expected gone: location, PC and user name, face tags, design-tool author and project.
Users reported what a cleaning left behind (PDF, AVIF) and files the app could not verify.
Users questioned the app's network and permission behaviour: a firewall prompt, a location-access question.
The app promises no network access, no telemetry and no automatic updates, and its code is open to check.
A false clean result is worse than a visible failure, because the file is shared believing the data is gone.
No issue in the tracker (213 read on 2026-11-11) is filed by someone who says they are a journalist or a source; this persona's existence rests on the brand book.

redFlags.text: A cleaned file that still carries an identifying field, such as a user name or a PC name.
Claims the app cannot prove, such as secure, anonymous or untraceable.
A PDF that still holds metadata after cleaning.
A failed-file message that does not say the original is unchanged.
Absolute promises the app cannot prove, such as one hundred percent secure or guaranteed.

jobs.when: I am about to post, send or sell a file
jobs.want: what it says about me gone before it leaves my hands
jobs.so: I can share it without giving away more than I meant

claims.text: Users asked about removing location, PC name and user name, and face data.

jobs.when: I clean a file I care about
jobs.want: the things I rely on, such as which way it faces, how its colour reads and how large it prints, to stay as they were
jobs.so: it works in my other tools afterwards and I do not repair it by hand

claims.text: Users reported rotation and resolution lost after cleaning and asked for options to keep rotation, resolution and the colour profile.

jobs.want: to see exactly what was removed and what remains
jobs.so: I can trust the result without checking it another way

claims.text: Users asked for the full list of removed metadata and were unsure about a count of 0.

jobs.when: a file could not be cleaned, or the result could not be checked
jobs.want: to be told plainly which file and what state it is in
jobs.so: I never believe a file is clean when it is not

claims.text: Users reported files the app could not verify, and cleaning that failed outright.

jobs.when: I am not sure a cleaning will go right
jobs.want: my original kept exactly as it was
jobs.so: I can try again or go back

claims.text: Users asked for a copy instead of an overwrite and reported an original modified with Save as copy on.

jobs.when: I have a whole folder or a large set to clean
jobs.want: to hand it over once and get through all of it
jobs.so: I am not cleaning file by file

claims.text: Users asked for folders, sub-folders and multi-file drops.

jobs.when: a large run finishes or is under way
jobs.want: to see which files are cleaned, which failed and which need a look, and to find the results
jobs.so: I know what to do next without opening each file

claims.text: The maintainer's own jobs list for results and output folders; no user report yet.

jobs.when: I hand the app personal or sensitive files
jobs.want: to know it stays on my computer and sends nothing out
jobs.so: I can use it for files I could not upload anywhere

claims.text: Users questioned the app's outbound connection and location access.

jobs.when: I open the app for the first time with a file in hand
jobs.want: one obvious thing to do and a result I can see
jobs.so: I get the file cleaned without help

claims.text: Users reported seeing nothing after a drop, and one reported that the app did not work and asked for help.
